p:cNvPr.descr: Two structures representing helix-turn-helix. In part a, there are two blue strands that cross each other, forming an X. The strand that starts from the top right and travels down and left curves upward to the top left, where it meets the beginning of the strand that goes from top left to bottom right. Some yellow lines with yellow hexagons dangle all around the inside portions of both strands. Below the X shape is a coiled, dark blue ribbon, labeled Helix. A light blue coiled ribbon attaches to the left corner of the dark blue ribbon, as well as to the bottom right of the X shape. In between the X and the coils is a purple thread-like structure looped on top of itself, labeled as “recognition helix.” Below it is a thin purple line, labeled, “Turn,” that connects to the right side of the dark blue coil. In part b, a short whiter arrow outlined in black points up to part a from a square box that contains two light blue coils. Below this box is a series of pink and red coils mixed together, with the pink heavily located on the right, and the red mostly on the left. To the top left are two light blue coils connected to two yellow coils at their right. To the right and below the pink and red coils are four green coils, labeled, “alpha helices involved in tetramer formation,” which are connected to a set of lighter red and darker red coils on the right. On top of them are two yellow coils, labeled as linker helices, and to their right are two light blue coils. To the top left of the linker helices are two additional light blue coils, labeled as DNA-binding domain.
